instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Back Me Up
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've marked Alex's name red, so I've marked it red on my copy. Back me up that the bins are his turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Red means he's away. That's why it's your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, his absence is the issue. Tell the house meeting he should arrange cover before he goes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can support that for next time, but tonight still needs doing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, say next time first. Then ask who can cover Alex tonight; don't introduce it as my regular job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said motion carried so firmly. I'll use that: the morning shift is mine, and the evening can go elsewhere. Back me up with the manager.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The motion was about moving the filing cabinet. Nobody voted on your shift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, moving things sensibly. You could support keeping my hours together in the morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can say it's a reasonable request. I can't say we agreed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say reasonable before I give the hours. Use that same certain voice; I'd like her to hear support, not a problem.

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You wrapped tape round that chair leg, so I've taped this loose one. Sit on it before I use it for dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My tape marks where to cut. It isn't holding anything together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, marking the weak point. You can test how it holds while I watch the tape.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You sit. I'll watch it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll steady the back for you. Just put a little weight on the seat first; I'll only take my turn once you've stood up again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You shook the coffee tin so confidently, so I've shaken this cheap substitute. Have the first sip before I fill my cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking whether my tin was empty. We've still got proper coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, checking the supply. If you like this, we can keep the proper stuff for visitors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not spoiling my breakfast for an experiment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sip, then. If it's awful, I'll get you proper coffee and a croissant. Mine can stay empty until you tell me.

cards.title: Count What I Did
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You wrote fragile on the glasses, so I've wrapped all twelve tins too. That was forty minutes of packing for your move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fragile means breakable. The tins didn't need wrapping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, protecting the contents. Twelve separate parcels, forty minutes. Could you tell the others I did those before they arrived?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll unwrap them myself. You can sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. When you take each wrapper off, tell them that was one I put on. I'd like the forty minutes counted before they're all in the bin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said feather the paint, so I've brushed these three fence boards with a feather. That took my whole Saturday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Feather means soften the edge with a brush. You've barely covered three boards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Soft edges, yes. Three boards took eighteen passes each. Please tell me you can see the work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll go over them with a proper brush. It won't take long.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the neighbours you went over my Saturday's work, then. Don't let your quick coat make it sound as though I never spent the day here.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put your call on hold, so I've put dinner on hold too. Do I finish your parents' gravy or drive you to the station?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Gravy doesn't pause. It needs stirring now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, keep it moving. Then choose: dinner ready for your parents, or your lift?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finish dinner. I'll book a taxi. Just carry my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Case downstairs now, or gravy without lumps? Pick one and I'll do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've starred the station on your phone, so I've starred the parcel depot too. Both urgent. Which am I collecting: your mum or her present?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The star saves an address. It doesn't mean urgent. Mum's already waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, saved for collection. The depot closes at six. Do you want Mum waiting for me or waiting for her present?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Get the present. I'll call Mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's calling me now. Do I stop to explain, or keep going before the depot closes? You choose.

cards.title: Move It for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've pencilled in your haircut, so I've pencilled lunch over it. Move the appointment for me; we've been friends since school.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in pencil because the salon changed the time, not because it doesn't matter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, room for changes. Couldn't an old friend have that slot just once?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'll charge twenty pounds if I change it today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll pay. Put lunch in that exact slot, in pen. I want one appointment with me that doesn't look ready to disappear.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said you can play your joker at the quiz. Use it to leave early for your sister's exhibition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The joker doubles points. It doesn't let the captain leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, double value. Your sister's first opening ought to count for more than one quiz night. Tell them you're coming to support me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave after round one and say I've got a headache.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come after round one, but say, 'I'm leaving for my sister's opening.' Let them find another captain for the rest.
